title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp. 75–77). A 'spatio' (Σ, ≤, C) is a poset with a map C satisfying axioms Spt 1–3. The intended meaning is a complete lattice with an orthocomplementation C: C is an order-reversing involution and x ∧ Cx = 0. A 'disjonction' (E, |0|) is a set with a symmetric relation (Disj 1). By Disj 2, self-disjoint elements form a 'null' part E_0, and A ∩ A^⊥ ⊂ E_0. Define the polar W(A) = A^⊥ = {y : y|0|a for all a ∈ A}. Then Σ_E is the set of biorthogonally closed subsets A = A^⊥⊥, ordered by inclusion, with C(A) = A^⊥. It is a complete ortholattice, i.e. a spatio. The canonical map σ_E : E → Σ_E sends x to {x}^⊥⊥.

On a spatio, the canonical disjunction is x|0|y ⇔ x ≤ Cy, which is equivalent to y ≤ Cx.

Proposition 1. For a spatio Σ with this disjunction, σ : Σ → Σ_Σ is an isomorphism of spatios, with inverse S ↦ sup S. Proof:
- {x}^⊥ = ↓Cx, so {x}^⊥⊥ = ↓x and σ(x) = ↓x.
- For any S, S^⊥ = ↓C(sup S), so S^⊥⊥ = ↓(sup S).
- Hence the closed sets are exactly the principal down-sets, σ is bijective, it preserves order, and C(↓x) = (↓x)^⊥ = ↓Cx.

Scholium. On a fixed set Σ there is a bijection between spatio structures (≤, C) and disjunction structures for which Σ → Σ_Σ is bijective. One direction takes a spatio to its associated disjunction. The other transports the spatio structure of Σ_Σ along the bijection.

Marginal notes recover the order and complement from the disjunction:
- x ≤ y ⇔ (∀z)(z|0|y ⇒ z|0|x);
- Cx = sup{y : x|0|y}.

Purpose. The page serves the next one (Proposition 2): characterising σ_E : E → Σ_E by a universal / uniqueness property, so that spatios become 'canonical disjunctions' and Σ_E the spatio canonically attached to any disjunction. This is the analogue of a MacNeille-type completion.
errors: No real error. Proposition 1 needs Σ to be a complete lattice (sup S for arbitrary S), presumably built into Spt 1–3.
In the Scholium, the round-trip check (the disjunction induced by the transported structure equals the original) is not written out. It holds: σ(x) ⊂ {y}^⊥ ⇔ x ∈ {y}^⊥, since {y}^⊥ is closed.
Bijectivity of Σ → Σ_Σ forces E_0 to have at most one element, i.e. the null part must reduce to a single bottom; this is left implicit.

ideas.what: Lattice of biorthogonally closed subsets of a set with a symmetric (orthogonality) relation is a complete ortholattice
ideas.modern_name: orthogonality space / orthoclosure, Galois connection of a symmetric relation

ideas.what: Every complete ortholattice is isomorphic to the closed-set lattice of its own orthogonality relation x ⊥ y ⇔ x ≤ y'; inverse S ↦ sup S
ideas.modern_name: representation of complete ortholattices via orthogonality spaces

ideas.what: Correspondence between ortholattice structures on a set and orthogonality relations whose canonical map to the closure lattice is bijective; recovery of order and complement from ⊥
ideas.modern_name: equivalence of complete ortholattices with 'reduced' complete orthogonality spaces

missed.claim: Historical: in July 1986 Grothendieck independently developed the theory of orthogonality spaces and complete ortholattices (his 'disjonctions' and 'spatios'), the structures of quantum logic, apparently without reference to that literature. Mathematically the content is classical.
missed.quote: l'application canonique σ : Σ → Σ_Σ est un isomorphisme de spatios. L'isomorphisme inverse est donné par σ^{-1} : S ↦ sup S
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents a lattice/orthogonality-based approach to 'space' in Grothendieck's late notes, of interest to historians tracing his post-1984 foundational projects. It is not new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct but classical (Birkhoff polarities, Dacey/MacLaren orthogonality spaces). The only mild interest is that Grothendieck rederived quantum-logic-style structures in 1986.
transcription_corrections: 'structure de disposition' / 'disp.' should read 'structure de disjonction' / 'disj.' (as on p. 75).
'|·|' throughout should be '|0|', the disjunction relation.
Top-left margin: 'Décrire la relation d'ordre can. en termes de disj.: x ≤ y ⇔ (∀z)(z|0|y ⇒ z|0|x)'.
Lower-left margin: 'D'autre part Cx = sup_{y∈Σ} y, où x|0|y' (i.e. Cx = sup{y : x|0|y}).
